audience: Trail and XC riders who want a hardtail mountain frame they built themselves — people who value durability and impact resistance on rough terrain over featherweight numbers, and who like that a bamboo frame is a genuine talking point on the trail.

positioning.title: A hardtail that soaks up the trail, not your wallet.
positioning.lede: Bigger bamboo tubes, tighter tolerances and disc-ready 29er geometry — built by hand to take roots, rocks and drops. Bamboo's natural damping kills trail chatter the way an alloy frame never will, and the joints are stronger than the tubes.

who_for.title: Trail & XC hardtail riders
who_for.body: Singletrack, roots and rock gardens on a rigid-rear frame. Disc-brake mounts and clearance for big off-road rubber.

who_for.title: Riders who want a frame that lasts
who_for.body: Under 1% failure across 4,000+ builds, 8–12 year life with care. Bamboo dents and repairs — it doesn't shatter on impact like carbon.

who_for.title: Builders who want the story
who_for.body: No experience needed — 95% of builders start with none. Roll up to the trailhead on a bamboo hardtail you built yourself.

faq.q: Can a bamboo frame really handle proper trail riding?
faq.a: Yes. Bamboo's natural damping is a real advantage on rough terrain, and the bonded joints are stronger than the tubes themselves. Riders hit singletrack, roots and drops on BBC hardtails regularly. Tested with Swansea University, under 1% failure across 4,000+ builds since 2012.

faq.q: Is it stiff enough to climb and put power down?
faq.a: The MTB kit uses bigger-diameter bamboo tubes and tighter tolerances than our road and gravel kits, built for off-road loads. Builders report it climbs well and descends confidently — 'the 29er geometry is spot on.'

faq.q: Will it survive impacts and rough terrain?
faq.a: Bamboo is a natural composite at roughly 28,000 PSI tensile strength — comparable to mild steel but lighter. Unlike carbon it doesn't fail catastrophically on a hard hit, and any damage can be repaired with epoxy anywhere in the world.

faq.q: What wheel size and brakes does it take?
faq.a: It's built around 29er geometry with disc-brake mounts and a BSA 68mm bottom bracket. Our MTB component pack is specced for 650B/27.5" if you prefer the smaller, punchier wheel — your call.

faq.q: How long does the MTB frame take to build?
faq.a: About 30–45 hours over a few weekends — a little longer than our road and gravel kits because the tubes are larger and the off-road tolerances are tighter. No power tools needed: just basic hand tools and a work surface.
